transcription.original_script:
№ 7
Попово
Состоялось въ Посадѣ Сероцкѣ одиннадцатаго (Двадцать тре-
тьяго) Февраля тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года, въ
два часа по полудни. — Явился лично Моисеева Закона Гас-
кель Соляржъ торговщикъ, Двадцать семи лѣтъ отъ роду въ Дере-
внѣ Поповѣ жительствующій, въ присутствіи свидѣтелей
Моисеева Закона Шмая Соляржа сапожника тридцати
семи лѣтъ отъ роду и Абрама Вайнгарда Школьника соро-
ка четырехъ лѣтъ отъ роду, здѣсь въ Сероцкѣ живущихъ,
и предъявилъ намъ младенца женскаго пола, объявляя, что
она родилась въ Деревнѣ Поповѣ шестаго (осьмнадца-
таго) Февраля текущаго года, въ семь часовъ
утра, отъ законной его жены Шейндла урожденной Прухъ. Двад-
цати семь лѣтъ отъ роду. Младенцу этому
Дано Имя Малка. Актъ сей объявляющему и свидѣтелямъ
прочитанъ, а затѣмъ объявляющимъ, свидѣтелями, а так-
же нами подписанъ — Chackel Solarsz
Abram Woingird    Szymaja Solarz
Содержащій Акты Гражданскаго Состоянія
transcription.translation: No. 7. Popowo. It took place in the Posad of Serock on the eleventh (twenty-third) of February, one thousand eight hundred seventy-seven, at two o'clock in the afternoon. There appeared in person Chackel Solarz, of the Mosaic faith, trader, twenty-seven years of age, residing in the village of Popowo, in the presence of the witnesses, of the Mosaic faith, Szymaja Solarz, shoemaker, thirty-seven years of age, and Abram Wajngard, synagogue attendant, forty-four years of age, both living here in Serock, and he presented to us an infant of female sex, declaring that she was born in the village of Popowo on the sixth (eighteenth) of February of the current year, at seven o'clock in the morning, of his lawful wife Szejndla, née Pruch, twenty-seven years of age. This infant was given the name Malka. This act was read to the declarant and the witnesses, and was thereupon signed by the declarant, by the witnesses, and also by us. Chackel Solarsz. Abram Woingird. Szymaja Solarz. Keeper of the Registers of Civil Status.

notes: CONTRADICTS THE BATCH BRIEF, which pins target.language = "pl". Russian in pre-reform orthography throughout the clerk's text.

This act is the cleanest in the group and was used as the reference for this clerk's letterforms when reading the fainter acts, in particular for establishing that the dual date is written as an ordinal followed by a parenthesised second ordinal.
Registration in the posad, while both the declarant's residence and the birthplace are the village of Popowo.
Read at 3.6x over source (480,245,1060,68) and again in band; fully legible without special measures.
Split across the line 1/2 break, with the parenthesis closed. Gap check: 11 to 23 February is 12 days, correct.
This is the instance of the dual-date slot that first made the clerk's pattern legible and it was then applied backwards to acts 1 and 2.
Both day-words physically inked, with a clear opening parenthesis.

registration_year.original_script: тысяча восемьсотъ семьдесятъ седьмаго года, въ

notes: часа по полудни is firm and places it in the afternoon; the numeral sits at the start of line 3 and reads два or три.
Given name split across the line 3/4 break at the page edge; quoted across the break as inked. Read at 7x over source (1150,366,380,58) and 6.5x over (476,413,560,58).

Corroborated by the declarant's own Latin-script autograph Chackel Solarsz, read at 3.9x over source (476,1015,1054,145). The autograph fixes both halves: Chackel for the split given name and Solarz for the surname.
The Cyrillic Гас- is normalised to Chackel rather than Haskiel here because the man's own signature spells it with Ch; the alternative preserves the other convention.
Not the same man as act 3's Гаскель Нейманъ, despite the shared given name: different surname, different trade, different residence.
Standard declarant-is-father construction. The word отецъ is not used on this act.
Same recurring fork as acts 4 and 5; the tail shows a щ-like descender.

declarant.age.original_script: Двадцать семи лѣтъ отъ роду въ Дере-
notes: Excerpt extended past роду because the act carries a second identical age phrase for the mother.
Split across the line 4/5 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Same village as acts 1, 4 and 5. On this act the letterforms of Поповѣ are unusually clean, which independently supports the Popowo reading adopted for act 1.
Same person as the declarant.

father.age.original_script: Двадцать семи лѣтъ отъ роду въ Дере-
notes: Father and mother are both given as twenty-seven on this act, which is internally consistent.
Read at 5.5x over source (476,507,700,58). Corroborated by the Latin autograph Szymaja Solarz.

A coarser band pass had misread this surname as Розенберга, on the assumption that the register's recurring shoemaker witness was appearing again; the signature block ruled that out. Worth recording because it is exactly the failure mode the within-register consistency check can cause if it is applied as an expectation rather than as a check.
Witness 1 shares the declarant's surname, which suggests a family connection, but the act does not state any relationship and none is asserted here.

witness_1.age.original_script:
сапожника тридцати
семи лѣтъ отъ роду
notes: Split across the line 6/7 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Plural phrase covering both witnesses. Note живущихъ here where other acts in the group use жительствующихъ.
Read in band at 3.8x. Абрама is firm and the surname opens Вайн-; the second element is the problem.

The Latin autograph reads Abram Woingird or Woingierd, which points to a -gard or -gird ending rather than the -berg I read on act 3 for what is almost certainly the same man, same trade, same age of forty-four.

IMPORTANT FOR ADJUDICATION: this fork should be resolved together with act 3's witness_1, where I recorded Abram Wajnberg. One of the two readings of that man's surname is wrong, and this act's autograph is the better evidence, but I have not retroactively rewritten act 3's body reading on that basis because act 3's own ink does support Вайнберга.
Both candidates retained here rather than one being chosen.
Capitalised by the clerk. Same fork as act 3 for the same man; the two candidates carry different occupational meanings.

соро-
ка четырехъ лѣтъ отъ роду, здѣсь
notes: Split across the line 7/8 break; quoted across the break as inked.
Witness-age continuity: the same man is given as forty-four in act 3 as well, registered a month earlier in the same register year. Clean agreement.
Read at 3.9x and 6.5x over source (476,927,1054,58) and (476,927,620,58). Both Дано and Имя are capitalised by the clerk.
Малка is short, fully formed and unambiguous, which is rare in this group. A female name, consistent with the stated female sex.
Read at 6x over source (900,648,630,58) after a coarser band pass had suggested a masculine что онъ родился; at 6x the presentation slot reads женскаго and the verb reads она родилась.
Corroborated by the female name Malka and by the absence of circumcision wording.
Read at 6x over source (900,695,630,58).
Split across the line 10/11 break, parenthesis closed. Gap check: 6 to 18 February is 12 days, correct.
Date arithmetic against the registration: born 6 February Julian, registered 11 February Julian, so registration follows the event by five days. Consistent, and no delay clause appears.
Both day-words inked.

child.birth_year.original_script: Февраля текущаго года, въ семь часовъ
notes: текущаго года rather than an explicit year, marking an in-time registration, in contrast to acts 4 and 5.
Split across the line 11/12 break; quoted across the break as inked.

child.birthplace.original_script: она родилась въ Деревнѣ Поповѣ шестаго
notes: Excerpt carries the following day-word to keep it unique. Agrees with the margin annotation and the declarant's residence.
Read at 7.5x over source (1050,792,480,58). Left uninflected by the clerk after жены.

Highest-value field on the act. Unusually short for this register: a single syllable plus the hard sign, written entirely on one line with no break, which removes the split-across-lines problem that afflicts acts 1, 4, 5 and 6.
Read at 7.5x over source (1050,792,480,58). The -ру- is firm. What is open is the initial, П or Б, and the penultimate letter, х or с.
Note that this is a plain surname, not one of the -овны or -овной patronymic forms seen on acts 3, 5 and 6.
Deliberately not completed to a more familiar surname.

mother.age.original_script:
Двад-
цати семь лѣтъ отъ роду. Младенцу этому
notes: Split across the line 12/13 break; quoted across the break and through the following words to distinguish it from the father's identical age.
The naming slot runs from Младенцу этому straight to Дано Имя Малка. No rite phrase: neither при обрѣзаніи, which would be wrong for a girl, nor при религіозномъ обрядѣ, which would be right.
BLANK rather than ABSENT_ON_FORM: the formula has the slot and this same clerk fills it on acts 1, 2, 3 and 6.
Verified by cropping the junction of the two lines at 6.5x over source (476,927,620,58) and 7.5x over (1150,883,380,58), to be sure the phrase had not been carried over the line break.

PATTERN ACROSS THE GROUP: this clerk omits the rite phrase on every female birth in acts 1 to 10 read so far, namely acts 4, 5 and 7, and includes при обрѣзаніи on every male birth. That is a systematic habit rather than three separate slips, and it means the omission carries information about sex rather than being noise.

signatures_note.value: Read to the declarant and witnesses and signed by the declarant, the witnesses and the registrar; three Latin-script autographs inked
signatures_note.original_script:
прочитанъ, а затѣмъ объявляющимъ, свидѣтелями, а так-
же нами подписанъ
notes: The clause includes объявляющимъ and there is no illiteracy note; all three parties signed.

Autographs read at 3.9x over source (476,1015,1054,145) as Chackel Solarsz, Abram Woingird and Szymaja Solarz. This is the most legible signature block in the group and it settled three separate name questions on this act.

It also bears on other acts: the surname here is plainly Solarz, which makes the Sołtarz reading I gave to the similar-looking autographs on acts 1, 4 and 5 doubtful. Those labels have been annotated accordingly.
